title: SEALSQ Reports H1 2026 Financial Results: Revenue Surges 131% to $11.2M, $486M Cash Balance, and Post-Quantum Hardware Progress - Quantum Computing Report
gist: SEALSQ (NASDAQ: LAES) more than doubled H1 2026 revenue to $11.15M with gross margin up 1,480bps to 48.5%, but operating expenses rose 64% to $37.57M for a $27.79M net loss, funded by a $495.0M cash and short-term investment position. The company reaffirmed FY2026 revenue guidance of $27M-$36M, cited a pipeline above $225M through 2029 with over $100M post-quantum, and is deploying a $200M SEALQUANTUM stack allocation into acquisitions of Miraex and Wecan plus investments in Quobly and EeroQ.

insights.claim: SEALSQ Corp generated $11.15 million of revenue in H1 2026, a 131.1% year-over-year increase from $4.83 million in H1 2025.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Triple-digit growth off a tiny base — the question is whether FY guidance of $27M-$36M implies acceleration or deceleration in H2.

insights.claim: Gross profit rose 232.6% to $5.41 million and gross margin expanded 1,480 basis points to 48.5%, attributed to improved product mix and high-margin ASIC engineering services.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Margin expansion driven by services mix, not chip volume — watch whether margins hold once hardware revenue dominates.

insights.claim: Operating expenses grew 64.3% to $37.57 million, including an 84.5% rise in R&D to $8.72 million for post-quantum product certifications and $23.10 million of G&A supporting corporate expansion and M&A integration.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: G&A at $23.1M is nearly triple R&D and more than double total revenue — an unusual cost structure that deserves scrutiny for a chip company.

insights.claim: GAAP net loss widened 38.7% to $27.79 million with an operating loss of $32.16 million, the gap partially mitigated by non-operating interest income earned on the company's substantial cash reserves.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Losses are growing faster than revenue; interest income on the cash pile is doing material work in the P&L, which reverses if rates fall.

insights.claim: Cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash of $486.1 million plus $8.9 million of current short-term investments totaled $495.0 million as of June 30, 2026, up 309.1% from $121.0 million a year earlier.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: At roughly $28M of semi-annual net loss, the balance sheet funds many years of burn — dilution risk is low but so is capital discipline pressure.
insights.locator: Cash and Short-Term Investments strictly aggregates

insights.claim: SEALSQ reports semi-annually under IFRS/U.S. GAAP as a foreign private issuer, so its results are compared against H1 2025 rather than a sequential quarter.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Semi-annual reporting means longer information gaps and more scope for surprises between prints — a volatility factor for the ticker.
insights.locator: Because SEALSQ reports semi-annually under IFRS

insights.claim: Revenue growth was driven by renewed demand for the Vault-IC secure-element family, expanding PKI subscription services, initial design revenue from the Quantix Edge Security center in Spain, and a full six-month consolidation of $2.5 million from custom ASIC designer IC'Alps, acquired in August 2025.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: $2.5M of the $6.3M revenue increase is acquired IC'Alps consolidation — organic growth is roughly half the headline number.
insights.locator: Revenue growth was driven by renewed demand

insights.claim: SEALSQ reaffirmed full-year FY 2026 revenue guidance of $27 million to $36 million, representing expected year-over-year growth of 50% to 100% over FY 2025.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hitting the low end requires roughly $16M in H2 versus $11.15M in H1; the top end requires nearly $25M — a wide, checkable spread.

insights.claim: Management cited an active business pipeline exceeding $225 million through 2029, with over $100 million tied directly to post-quantum projects.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Pipeline-through-2029 figures are soft, non-GAAP disclosures; the conversion rate from pipeline to booked revenue is the real metric to track.
insights.locator: Management cited an active business pipeline

insights.claim: The QS7001 Quantum Shield chip achieved NIST Entropy Source Validation under ESV Certificate #E333 for SP 800-90B entropy certification.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Formal NIST validation is a procurement gate for government and defense buyers — it unlocks addressable market rather than just marketing claims.

insights.claim: SEALSQ completed key fault-injection and side-channel attack testing required for Common Criteria EAL5+ security evaluation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: EAL5+ is the certification level required for payment, identity and government smartcard sockets — progress here maps to design wins.

insights.claim: Engineering samples of the QVault TPM-185 were made available to over 30 evaluating prospective customers and partners as of June 30, 2026, with initial commercial revenue from QS7001 and QVault TPM expected toward the end of H2 2026 and scaling into 2027.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Flagship product revenue is still ahead, not behind — H1's growth came from legacy and acquired lines, so 2027 is the real proof point.

insights.claim: SEALSQ has committed more than $60 million of its $200 million SEALQUANTUM Sovereign Vertical Stack allocation to build an integrated post-quantum hardware ecosystem, leaving roughly $140 million uncommitted.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals a continued acquisition cadence in post-quantum and quantum hardware — SEALSQ is an active bidder to price into private valuations.

insights.claim: SEALSQ finalized a 100% acquisition of Miraex SA to integrate quantum-photonic interconnect technology and acquired a 55.5% controlling stake in Wecan Group for AI-powered post-quantum compliance and digital identity solutions.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A chip company buying photonic interconnect and compliance software is building a stack, not a product — integration execution risk rises accordingly.

insights.claim: SEALSQ participated as a lead investor in Quobly's €115 million Series A and expanded financial commitments to electrons-on-helium quantum developer EeroQ.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A €115M Series A for Quobly is a datapoint on silicon-spin qubit private valuations; SEALSQ is turning into a quasi-venture vehicle alongside its chip business.
